title: Accelerating vision-language models with LFM2.5-VL-DSpark
gist: Liquid AI released an experimental 280M-parameter DSpark speculative-decoding drafter for its LFM2.5-VL-3B vision-language model, delivering up to 3.13x decode speedup on an M5 Max and up to 2.66x on H100 (2.62x/2.27x end-to-end) for an 8.9% parameter overhead, with day-one llama.cpp, MLX-VLM and SGLang support. The team flags that on edge devices vision encoding and prefill dominate latency, capping end-to-end gains per Amdahl's law.

insights.claim: Liquid AI's DSpark drafter for LFM2.5-VL-3B yields decode speedups up to 3.13x on device and 2.66x on an Nvidia H100, with end-to-end gains up to 2.62x and 2.27x respectively, without changing output quality.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Speculative decoding is extending from text LLMs to VLMs, cutting inference cost per token for multimodal edge and server workloads.

insights.claim: With MLX on an Apple M5 Max, DSpark speeds decoding 2.30x to 3.13x by task and end-to-end latency 1.56x to 2.62x, while llama.cpp on an M3 Ultra improves decoding 1.57x to 2.14x and end-to-end 1.30x to 1.77x, measured on six MMSpec-style vision tasks at block size 8.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Apple silicon, especially M5, is a strong target for on-device multimodal inference; gains vary widely by runtime and chip generation.

insights.claim: The article reports H100 decode speedups as '20.4x to 2.66x' alongside 1.64x to 2.27x end-to-end, which is almost certainly a typo (likely 2.04x) given the 2.66x headline maximum.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Do not cite the 20.4x figure; datacenter gains are roughly 2-2.7x decode, lower than on-device.
insights.quote: On H100, the same drafter delivers 20.4x to 2.66x faster decoding

insights.claim: The vision DSpark drafter adds about 279.5M parameters (193.0M 4-layer decoder, 21.0M hidden-state projection, 65.5M Markov head), only 8.9% on top of the 3B target model.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Small memory overhead for 2-3x decode gains makes speculative decoding attractive on memory-constrained edge devices.

insights.claim: Because image patches and text tokens are projected into a shared hidden-state representation, the same DSpark drafter design used for Liquid AI's text models works unchanged for vision: it taps target-model hidden states at fixed layers to draft blocks of k tokens.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Modality-agnostic drafters lower the cost of extending speedups across a model family, a scaling advantage for Liquid AI's product line.
insights.locator: How does speculative decoding work for VLMs

insights.claim: Ablations across 3, 4 and 5 layers led to a simplified attention-only 4-layer drafter with block size 9, trained 10 epochs on a vision-language SFT mixture weighted toward expected workloads, with acceptance improving until diminishing returns.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Drafter quality is workload-tuned, so speedups may be lower on out-of-distribution tasks.

insights.claim: Speculative decoding accelerates only the decode stage, not vision encoding or prefill, so when those stages dominate wall time a large decode speedup gives only a modest end-to-end gain.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Headline decode-speedup claims overstate user-visible gains for image-heavy workloads; prefill/encoder compute remains the edge bottleneck.
insights.quote: This is Amdahl's law, where the overall speedup is capped by the part of the workload that isn't accelerated.
insights.locator: Limitations of speculation for vision workloads

insights.claim: On edge devices prefill takes a larger share of VLM latency than on datacenter GPUs because the vision encoder plus hundreds of visual tokens are compute-bound, though the Apple M5's per-core GPU neural accelerators narrow this gap.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Dedicated neural accelerators in client silicon (like M5) directly unlock better on-device multimodal AI; a hardware differentiator to watch.
insights.quote: The M5's per-core GPU neural accelerators narrow this gap
insights.locator: Limitations of speculation for vision workloads

insights.claim: Liquid AI shipped the vision drafter with day-one integrations for llama.cpp, MLX-VLM and SGLang (via specific pull requests), in Safetensors and GGUF formats, positioning LFM2.5 as an open-weight model family that 'runs anywhere'.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Liquid AI is competing on open-weight edge efficiency and runtime ecosystem reach rather than frontier scale.

insights.claim: DSpark speculative decoding is exact: the target model verifies every proposed token, so greedy output equals the target model alone.
insights.speaker: xx
insights.so_what: Lossless speedups can be adopted in production without re-validating model quality, easing enterprise uptake.
insights.locator: The block size is read from the sidecar metadata
